title: Bus Driver Salary Melbourne: Award Rates, Casual Loading & Take-Home Pay
description: Discover the bus driver salary Melbourne rates under the Passenger Vehicle Award. Calculate annual, fortnightly pay, casual loading, super, and tax for 2026-27.
salarySummary: A full-time bus driver in Melbourne under the Passenger Vehicle Transportation Award Grade 1 earns $27.34 per hour, or $1,038.80 per week for 38 hours, with super and tax varying by circumstances.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a bus driver in Melbourne?
faqs.a: Under the Passenger Vehicle Transportation Award 2020, the minimum hourly rate for a Grade 1 full-time bus driver is $27.34 per hour as of 1 July 2026. This equates to $1,038.80 per week for 38 ordinary hours. Higher grades (Grade 2 to Grade 6) attract higher rates, up to $33.70 per hour for Grade 6. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate, making the casual Grade 1 rate $34.18 per hour.

faqs.q: How is casual loading calculated for bus drivers?
faqs.a: Casual loading under the Passenger Vehicle Transportation Award is 25% of the minimum hourly rate for the classification. For a Grade 1 bus driver, the base rate is $27.34 per hour, so the casual loading adds $6.84 per hour, resulting in a total casual rate of $34.18 per hour. This loading is paid for all ordinary hours worked and is intended to compensate for entitlements like paid leave. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply it in calculations.

faqs.q: What tax and super apply to a bus driver's salary?
faqs.a: For the 2026-27 financial year, resident tax rates apply: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of the salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, a Grade 1 full-time bus driver earning $54,017.60 annually would have super of about $6,482.11 added by the employer. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool to estimate net income after tax and Medicare.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Bus Driver Salary Melbourne

If you are researching **bus driver salary Melbourne**, the most reliable starting point is the Passenger Vehicle Transportation Award 2020, which sets minimum pay rates for drivers of buses, coaches, and minibuses across Australia, including Melbourne. This award is published by the Fair Work Ombudsman and updated after each Annual Wage Review. The current rates apply from 1 July 2026.

### How Annual Pay Is Calculated

Annual gross pay is calculated using the formula:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee, the award defines ordinary hours as an average of 38 per week. So a Grade 1 bus driver earning $27.34 per hour would have:

$27.34 × 38 × 52 = $54,017.60 per year

This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. If you work overtime or on weekends, penalty rates apply (e.g., 150% on Saturday, 200% on Sunday for non-two-driver operations). The [timesheet](/) can help you convert your actual hours and rate into annual, monthly, and fortnightly figures.

### Fortnightly Pay

A full-time bus driver paid fortnightly would receive:

$27.34 × 38 × 2 = $2,077.84 gross per fortnight (before tax and other deductions)

This is simply weekly pay multiplied by two. Many employers pay fortnightly, and the award requires payment no later than Thursday in the pay period.

### Award Rates for Bus Drivers

The award classifies bus drivers into six grades based on skill and responsibility. The minimum weekly and hourly rates from 1 July 2026 are:

| Grade | Weekly rate (38 hours) | Hourly rate |
|-------|------------------------|-------------|
| Grade 1 | $1,038.80 | $27.34 |
| Grade 2 | $1,062.90 | $27.97 |
| Grade 3 | $1,122.80 | $29.55 |
| Grade 4 | $1,162.40 | $30.59 |
| Grade 5 | $1,226.30 | $32.27 |
| Grade 6 | $1,280.50 | $33.70 |

These are minimum rates; some employers may pay above award. The [pay guides](/blog) page provides links to official pay guides for this award.

### Casual Loading

Casual bus drivers receive a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate. For a Grade 1 casual driver:

$27.34 × 1.25 = $34.18 per hour

This loading is paid for all ordinary hours and is intended to compensate for entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave that permanent employees receive. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply the loading correctly in your calculations.

### Superannuation

Under the award and the Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992, employers must pay superannuation contributions on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a Grade 1 full-time driver earning $54,017.60, the employer would contribute approximately $6,482.11 annually. This is not deducted from your salary; it is paid in addition. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more details on how super interacts with salary packaging.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

For the 2026-27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Using the Grade 1 annual salary of $54,017.60, the estimated tax (excluding offsets) would be:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000 ($26,800): 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $54,017.60 ($9,017.60): 30% = $2,705.28
- Total tax: $6,725.28
- Medicare levy (2%): $1,080.35
- Total tax and Medicare: $7,805.63
- Net annual income: $54,017.60 - $7,805.63 = $46,211.97

This is an estimate only. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool can calculate your net pay more precisely, including the tax-free threshold and any offsets.

### Other Allowances and Penalties

Bus drivers may be entitled to additional payments:

- **Articulated bus allowance**: $17.52 per shift when driving an articulated bus.
- **Meal allowance**: $17.41 when working more than 2 hours overtime beyond ordinary finishing time.
- **First aid allowance**: $21.33 per week if you hold a first aid certificate and are appointed by the employer.
- **Vehicle allowance**: $1.00 per km if you use your own vehicle for work.

Penalty rates for ordinary hours worked on weekends and public holidays are higher. For example, a Grade 1 driver on Sunday earns 200% of the minimum rate ($54.68 per hour) for ordinary hours. The [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page provides a breakdown of typical earnings including penalties.

### Comparing to National Minimum Wage and Average Earnings

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). The Grade 1 bus driver rate of $27.34 is above the minimum wage. For context, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time earnings was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which is higher than the award rates for bus drivers. However, many bus drivers receive overtime, penalty rates, and allowances that can increase total earnings.

### Work-Related Deductions

The Australian Taxation Office provides specific guidance for bus drivers on claiming deductions for work-related expenses. Common deductions include the cost of uniforms, protective clothing, tools, and licensing fees. You can also claim a portion of mobile phone and internet expenses if you use them for work. Keep receipts and a logbook for vehicle expenses if you use your own car for work purposes.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

To estimate your own **bus driver salary Melbourne** figures, use [the timesheet](/) on this site. Enter your base hourly rate (do not include casual loading; use the checkbox to add it), your weekly hours, and the tool will calculate annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. The calculator uses the 2026-27 tax rates and the 12% super guarantee rate.

### Summary

A full-time Grade 1 bus driver in Melbourne earns a minimum of $27.34 per hour under the Passenger Vehicle Transportation Award. Annual gross pay for 38 hours per week is $54,017.60. Casual drivers receive a 25% loading, making the hourly rate $34.18. Superannuation of 12% is paid on top, and tax is calculated using the resident tax scales plus Medicare levy. For a precise estimate of your take-home pay, including any allowances or penalties, refer to the [reference tables](/data) and the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for the latest rates.
